frequency_question: How often do structural federal-subnational friction points prevent the timely renewal of expiring transboundary water treaties within their final negotiation windows?
membership_rule: Includes formal bilateral or multi-state treaties governing shared river basins where an expiring treaty requires legislative or subnational consensus for renewal; excludes purely domestic water pacts and treaties without fixed expiration dates.

cases.name: Indus Waters Treaty implementation adjustments / Tulbul Navigation project talks (1984-1990s)
Colorado River Basin Minute negotiations between US and Mexico (Minute 319 / 323)
Nam Theun / Mekong basin upstream-downstream procedural protocol renewals
Senegal River Basin Development Organisation (OMVS) structural protocol updates

coverage_note: 5 major federal/asymmetric transboundary water renegotiation cases named; representative of the global class of federal subnational water frictions.
known_gaps: Excludes minor bilateral sub-basin agreements in Central Asia and Eastern Europe due to lack of granular subnational friction documentation.
skeleton: Transboundary basin renewal attempts complicated by subnational friction (5 distinct treaty renewal case environments identified since 1970)
multiplier: 3 hits out of 5 historical instances where structural friction threatened timely renewal
validity_reason: Base rate reflects long-term structural dynamics of federal-subnational friction in water governance, which evolves slowly over decades.
